- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce overshoot by 10–15% in subsequent periods.  
- If sentiment is neutral or weak (0.0–0.2), model should not deviate more than ±5% from recent 7-day average.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 10%+ above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–8% in next 5–7 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-leveraging bullish bias.  
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., >0.7) should trigger a 3–5 day lag correction in forecast to avoid premature overreaction.
